text:
The Canucks hadn't won in ten games (0-9-1), and for two periods and most of a third it looked like number eleven. Down 5-2 with less than eight minutes left, Vancouver scored four times, two of them from Jonathan Lekkerimäki, to tie it, and Filip Hronek won it on a power-play slap shot in overtime. That ended the skid with a 6-5 comeback from three goals down.

The scoreboard never matched the game. Our expected goals, a measure of the quality of chances, had VAN at 4.58 to ANA's 2.96, and the Canucks took 63 shot attempts to 42. By our simulations, which replay every shot, Vancouver deserved to win 80 percent of the time. The Ducks got ahead by making their few good looks count: A.J. Greer, Jeff Malott and Leo Carlsson scored in a second period that VAN dominated 1.79 to 0.99 in expected goals. Goalie Leevi Meriläinen allowed 2.6 more goals than his shots deserved, while Lukas Dostal turned aside a 28 percent look from Linus Karlsson that would have changed the middle of the night.

Lekkerimäki's tying goal came on a 3 percent chance, the least likely of the game. Jackson LaCombe, a 2019 second-round pick out of Minnesota, played 28:48 and set up three Ducks goals, and still finished on the wrong side of it. Vancouver finally has a win and a reason to exhale. Anaheim threw away a three-goal lead, and our numbers say the Ducks were closer to lucky than good for most of the first 57 minutes.
